title: Workload Categorizer + Cost Sentinel for Safe Continuous Batching
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a workload categorization and cost sentinel subsystem that recommends continuous batching parameters and safely applies/rolls back changes. The subsystem must profile incoming request streams, compute confidence-scored batch configs per workload class, run simulated dry-runs against historical traces, and perform transactional applies with automated rollback triggers when SLO or quality regressions are detected. This ticket focuses on the engine, heuristics library, and safe apply path; a follow-up will add a Console UI for manual review and overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Categorizer groups requests into distinct workload buckets (e.g., short-chat, long-context, high-embedding-rate) with <10% misclassification on test set
Engine produces recommended continuous batching params (max_batch, min_latency_ms, kv_cache_ttl, prefix_cache_enabled) per bucket with an accompanying confidence score
A simulated dry-run mode can replay 72 hours of historical traffic and estimate cost delta and p95/p99 latency impact per recommendation
Apply path uses a transactional two-phase deploy to runtime-config with canary fraction support and auto-rollback rules
Rollback triggers include latency SLO breach (p99 increase > 20%), cost anomaly (>15% unexpected increase), or quality regression measured by prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity sentinel sets
End-to-end telemetry and dashboard tiles exist: per-bucket recommended vs active config, estimated vs realized cost delta, rollback events
Automated safety net: a fast path to revert to the last golden config within 30s of a rollback decision
tasks: Define workload feature set and labeling rules (request size, model, route, user-agent, embedding vs. generation)
Implement lightweight profiler that emits per-window histograms and sample traces to S3/trace-store
Train and validate workload clustering + classification prototype (offline)
Develop heuristics library that maps workload fingerprints to batching parameter proposals
Add dry-run simulator that replays traces against candidate configs and computes cost/latency/quality estimates
Implement transactional apply in runtime-config service with canary fraction and watch hooks
Implement rollback detector running in control plane that evaluates live telemetry vs simulated expectations
Wire telemetry into Console experiment tiles and cost dashboard
Write integration tests and chaos tests that validate rollback and golden-config recovery
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: (1) Offline evaluation and internal sigmoids with synthetic traffic (2) Dry-run mode for a single non-critical customer cohort (canary 1%) for 48h (no auto-apply) (3) Enable auto-apply with conservative canary (5%) and strict rollback thresholds for 7 days (4) Gradually increase coverage with expanded workload buckets and tuned heuristics. Each stage requires sign-off from SRE and Product.
risks: Over-aggressive batching can increase p99 latency for tail requests if buckets are misclassified
Quality regressions for structured-output workloads if KV cache/partial-prefix caching is misapplied
Incorrect cost estimates from dry-run due to non-deterministic model runtime behavior or variability in kernel scheduling
Operational complexity for safe transactional applies—requires careful integration with Dedicated and Private runtimes
notes: Goal is conservative first: prioritize safety and explainability over maximal token savings
Design heuristics to fall back to global default config when confidence < 0.6
Dry-run should simulate KV cache warmup and prefix cache hit curves to estimate steady-state behavior
Consider adding a 'freeze window' to prevent auto-applies during peak traffic events (e.g., Black Friday)
